cases.title: A Min of 0 on a floating-point simulation is honoured, not replaced by the smallest denormal
cases.intent: Guards the minValueForType fix. It used to return Double.MIN_VALUE, which is the smallest POSITIVE denormal (4.9E-324), not the most negative double. Callers use it as a lower clamp via maxOf(), so any configured Min <= 0 was silently discarded and a "Min": 0 square wave oscillated between 4.9E-324 and Max instead of between 0 and Max. Note the assertion is set MEMBERSHIP, not a numeric range: 4.9E-324 lies inside [0, 100], so a range check would have passed the bug. Float is included because it had the same defect via Float.MIN_VALUE.

assert.comment: Membership, not range. Square is a function of wall clock, so a short window may legitimately observe only one of the two levels - which is why this is not channelValueSet.

cases.title: Range walks its values in order; List and nested Structure compose their items
cases.intent: Composite simulations model multi-value and structured device data. Range without Random advances an index per read and wraps (Range.kt:28-35); List evaluates every item each read and converts it to the List's DataType; Structure evaluates every property, recursively. The embedded counters are bounded (0..3) so their progress can be asserted as an exact cycle inside a list element and inside a structure, and the nested structure must arrive as a nested JSON object in every mode.

cases.title: A Counter channel produces a gap-free ascending sequence from Min
cases.intent: The foundation every other deterministic case rests on. Counter.next() returns the current value and then advances, and SimulatorSource calls it once per channel per read, so the emitted sequence is a function of read count alone - not of wall-clock time. If this case is not exact, no count-gated assertion elsewhere can be trusted. It also proves the whole harness path end to end: config placeholder substitution, the file sink as a record counter, and SFC's own metrics reaching the JSONL writer.

assert.comment: Valid here because the file sink preserves pipeline order. Over a queue this would be channelValueRun instead.
The fingerprint of a dependency version split. These leave the process exiting 0, so nothing else would notice.

cases.title: Counter direction, step, wrap-around, negative range, Float step and array Size
cases.intent: Counters drive most deterministic test data in SFC deployments and in this suite. Counter.next() returns the current value and then steps; UP wraps to Min when the next step would exceed Max, DOWN starts at Max and wraps to Max when it would go below Min, and Size > 0 fills an array by calling next() once per element. Every variant is a pure function of the read count, so each channel must follow its exact cycle in every mode: an off-by-one at the wrap, a DOWN counter starting at Min, a Float step rounded to Int or an array that repeats one value would all break a cycle.

cases.title: JSON representation of every simulator data type and of a Structure
cases.intent: Every consumer depends on the JSON type of each value. The simulator converts the configured value with SimulationHelper.asNumericType, and ChannelDataOutputSerializer writes Number/String/Boolean/Char directly and everything else through JsonHelper's adapters: UByte, UShort and UInt become JSON strings, ULong becomes a double, a Char a one-letter string and a Structure a JSON object. strictTypes makes 5000000000 vs 5.0E9 or 7 vs '7' a failure. In-process and uberjar only: the IPC adapter transport encodes the unsigned types as signed numbers, pinned by CORE-SIM-DATATYPES-02.

cases.title: IPC adapter transport encodes unsigned simulator values as signed numbers, so their JSON type differs from in-process (known defect)
cases.intent: The IPC-mode half of CORE-SIM-DATATYPES-01, with the same configuration. The gRPC ChannelValue message has unsigned fields and sfc-main decodes them (GrpcSourceValueAsNativeExt.kt:44), but the adapter service encodes UByte and UShort with toInt() and UInt and ULong with toLong() (GrpcSourceValueFromNativeExt.kt:110,195,280,365). sfc-main therefore receives signed values and writes 200, 60000, 4000000000 and 5 where an in-process deployment of the same configuration writes "200", "60000", "4000000000" and 5.0, so a consumer validating types breaks when the deployment mode changes. All other types are asserted equal to the in-process representation, which also proves Char and Structure survive the IPC hop.

assert.comment: Boolean True: the same as in-process

knownDefect.summary: The IPC adapter service encodes UByte/UShort as Int and UInt/ULong as Long instead of the ChannelValue unsigned fields, so IPC deployments emit 200/60000/4000000000/5 where in-process emits "200"/"60000"/"4000000000"/5.0

cases.title: A Constant simulation with an array Value, as documented, invalidates the whole simulator configuration (known defect)
cases.intent: docs/adapters/simulator.md:320,365,456 document a Constant whose Value is an array ('Simulation returning array of bytes'), and Constant.value() even handles a List. But Constant.fromJson converts the value with asType(), which has no list branch and calls asDouble() on the list, so the documented configuration raises 'must be a number'; the simulator wraps it in an InvalidSimulation, SimulatorChannelConfiguration.validate rejects it, the adapter is not created and SFC idles with no output - including the perfectly valid 'ctr' channel next to it. The case settles for a fixed time and pins that nothing is written; when fixed, records flow and arr is [1, 2, 3]. In-process and uberjar only: in IPC mode the same error surfaces through the adapter service's initialisation, which races with the known first-stream gRPC UNKNOWN retry (it appeared after 1 s in one run and not within 12 s in the next), so a fixed settle cannot observe it reliably; the defect is in the simulator's own parsing, identical in every mode.

wait.comment: Today SFC idles and nothing can be waited for; a log wait would turn a fix into a timeout ERROR instead of a FAIL. A fixed SFC delivers its first records within about 1 s in these modes.

knownDefect.summary: Constant.fromJson passes an array Value to asType(), which has no list branch (Constant.kt:29-50) and throws 'must be a number'; the documented array Constant disables the whole simulator adapter

cases.title: A DateTime simulation value is written as Gson's reflective dump of java.time.ZonedDateTime internals, not as a timestamp (known defect)
cases.intent: DateTime.value() returns a java.time.ZonedDateTime. JsonHelper registers a type adapter for Instant only, so ChannelDataOutputSerializer's fallback serialises the object reflectively and consumers receive the private field structure {dateTime: {date, time}, offset: {totalSeconds}, zone: {id}} - an implementation detail of the JDK - instead of an ISO-8601 value (in IPC mode the custom-value hop even turns its integers into doubles). The research claim that serialisation fails and the message is dropped is refuted on Corretto 21: records are delivered, which the case asserts, so the pin is the shape. The control schedule proves SFC is otherwise healthy; the DateTime schedule's counter proves its messages are complete.

knownDefect.summary: DateTime.value() returns java.time.ZonedDateTime, for which no Gson adapter is registered (JsonHelper.kt:171-183), so the value is serialised reflectively as the JDK's private fields {dateTime, offset, zone} instead of a timestamp

cases.title: Interval yields a value only every N ms; Buffered emits each buffered value as its own record
cases.intent: Interval and Buffered model devices that report sporadically or in bursts. Interval returns its item's next value once the interval has elapsed and null otherwise, so the inner counter advances only on emission: iv is a gap-free sequence from 0 over the records that contain it, and an Interval of an hour never appears. Buffered collects one (timestamp, value) pair per read and returns the batch once its interval elapses; ScheduleReader.sliceResults turns a list of ChannelReadValue into one result per element, so every buffered value arrives as its own record with a scalar value, gap-free across batches. Emission timing is wall-clock, so only presence and gap-free order are asserted; in-process the reads between batches also emit sourceless messages (CORE-OUT-NULLS-01), which skipMissing ignores.

assert.comment: A list value (no slicing) would fail as not numeric.

cases.title: An invalid simulation (Counter without DataType) is reported and disables the simulator, but the error names it "Companion" (known defect)
cases.intent: Simulation errors must be visible and must say what is wrong. Counter.fromJson returns an InvalidSimulation when DataType is missing, SimulatorChannelConfiguration.validate turns it into a ConfigurationException, the simulator adapter is not created and nothing is written (SFC then idles; that defect is pinned by CORE-SCHED-IDLE-01 and not asserted here). Known defect: every simulation's fromJson takes its name from this::class.java.simpleName inside the companion object, which is 'Companion', so the message reads 'SimulationType "Companion" is not valid' and does not name the simulation type. The case waits for the reason text, which a fix would keep.

wait.log: Simulation must have a data type in property DataType

wait.comment: Give a (wrongly) running simulator the time to write something; no condition can observe 'nothing happens'.

assert.text: is not valid, Simulation must have a data type in property DataType

knownDefect.summary: Simulation.fromJson implementations name the InvalidSimulation with this::class.java.simpleName inside the companion object, i.e. 'Companion', so validation errors say 'SimulationType "Companion" is not valid' instead of naming the simulation

cases.title: Wall-clock and random simulations stay within [Min, Max]; Random Double overshoots Max (known defect)
cases.intent: Sinus, Sawtooth and Triangle are functions of wall-clock time and Random is random, so only ranges and types can be asserted: Sawtooth and Triangle clamp to [Min, Max], Sinus oscillates within it, and Random Int draws from [Min, Max) as documented. Known defect: Random Double draws from nextDouble(Min, Max + 1), so a [0, 1] channel yields values up to 2. With 30 draws the chance that none exceeds 1 is 2^-30, so the pin discriminates; rd has its own source and sink so the raw scan for a value starting with '1.' can only match rd.

knownDefect.summary: Random with DataType Double draws from nextDouble(Min, Max + 1), so values exceed the configured Max by up to 1

assertCurrent.comment: At least one of 30 draws for Min 0 / Max 1 lies in [1, 2).
